idiom_name: JSON.parse followed by a tag-keyed dispatch table (or a reviver for nested values)
implementation_notes: JSON carries no type information and JSON.parse always produces plain objects, so the whole structure is written by hand: read the discriminator from the parsed value and look it up in a decoder table (a Map, or an object created with Object.create(null) so no prototype members can be hit). The reviver argument of JSON.parse can rebuild nested class instances while the document is walked and is the closest thing to a hook, but top-level dispatch belongs after parsing because a reviver visits children before their parent. Where class identity is not needed, returning the validated plain object is simpler than reconstructing prototypes that the serializer would strip again.
pitfalls: A plain object used as the dispatch table inherits from Object.prototype, so type: "constructor" or "toString" resolves to a member instead of failing; use Object.create(null) or a Map.

JSON.parse yields plain objects, so class identity must be restored explicitly: JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(x)) and structuredClone both discard prototypes and methods, and structuredClone throws on functions.
JavaScript numbers are IEEE-754 doubles, so integer ids above 2^53 are silently rounded during JSON.parse - keep large identifiers as strings in the payload.
